NASA. The National Aeronautics and Space Administration is the United States civilian space agency founded in nineteen fifty-eight during the Cold War, initially as a response to Soviet space achievements. It became the primary architect of American spaceflight and planetary exploration, coordinating the Mercury, Gemini, and Apollo programs, the Space Shuttle, and robotic missions throughout the solar system.

NASA was founded on October first, nineteen fifty-eight, by President Eisenhower, absorbing the earlier National Advisory Committee for Aeronautics in direct response to Sputnik. The agency organized the Mercury program from nineteen fifty-eight to nineteen sixty-three to put the first American in space and demonstrate manned spaceflight capability. John Glenn orbited Earth in nineteen sixty-two. It then directed the Gemini program from nineteen sixty-one to nineteen sixty-six to develop essential techniques for lunar landing: spacewalk, rendezvous, docking, and long-duration flight.

The agency orchestrated the Apollo program under President Kennedy's mandate to land humans on the Moon before the Soviet Union. Apollo eleven achieved this on July twentieth, nineteen sixty-nine. NASA sent twelve astronauts to the lunar surface across six successful missions—Apollo eleven, twelve, fourteen, fifteen, sixteen, and seventeen—validating lunar exploration and inspiring global scientific effort.

NASA developed the Space Shuttle program from nineteen eighty-one to twenty-eleven, the first reusable orbital spacecraft, which launched hundreds of missions and enabled construction of the International Space Station in partnership with Russia, Europe, Japan, and Canada. The agency has led robotic planetary exploration with Voyager one and two, interstellar probes launched in nineteen seventy-seven; Viking landers on Mars; the Hubble Space Telescope, deployed in nineteen ninety; and Mars rovers including Curiosity and Perseverance, as well as missions to every planet. NASA's institutional role—balancing scientific discovery, technological innovation, and geopolitical ambition—has made it central to how humans understand the cosmos and their place in it.
